correctness.rationale: Explicit 11-vertex adjacency-list construction matches the standard Herschel graph (18 edges, degrees eight 3s and three 4s, characteristic spectral pattern). Every Hamiltonian path has a red endpoint. Depth-first search exhaustively explores all red-starting simple spanning vertex sequences; a separate independent search tests all 43,758 10-edge subsets for connected path degree pattern. Both yield 222 unordered paths. In a graph with no Hamiltonian cycle, one-edge spanning-path exchange coincides with endpoint Pósa rotation. Both checkers construct all 444 edges; BFS from each of 222 states reaches all states and gives radius 8, diameter 9, ecc distribution 198/24. Exact instructions and stdout are included. The proof that every state has four neighbors uses the two unused edges at each degree-three red endpoint.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the extremal smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph. Its Hamiltonian paths exist but cannot close to a Hamiltonian cycle, making the reconfiguration of all spanning paths under the Pósa move a natural question. The finding gives a nontrivial complete answer: all 222 paths lie in one 4-regular reconfiguration component and transform within nine moves, with exact optimal worst-case distance and eccentricity distribution. This is a motivated complete finite invariant, not a random slice or generalization by renaming. No broader graph-family theorem is claimed.
